preconditions.description: The number of users n is between 2 and 250,000.
There are exactly n-1 edges in T1.
There are exactly n-1 edges in T2.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n for a, b in edges_T1)
preconditions.description: All edges in T1 connect valid user indices.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= c <= n and 1 <= d <= n for c, d in edges_T2)
preconditions.description: All edges in T2 connect valid user indices.

postconditions.description: The number of edges that can be protected is between 0 and n-1.
The number of protected edges matches the output count m.

postconditions.expression: all((a, b) in edges_T1 for a, b, c, d in protected_edges)
postconditions.description: Each protected edge in T1 is a valid edge from T1.

postconditions.expression: all((c, d) in edges_T2 for a, b, c, d in protected_edges)
postconditions.description: Each replacement edge in T2 is a valid edge from T2.

postconditions.expression: all(len(set(a for a, b, c, d in protected_edges)) == len(protected_edges))
postconditions.description: Each edge in T1 is used at most once for protection.

postconditions.expression: all(len(set(c for a, b, c, d in protected_edges)) == len(protected_edges))
postconditions.description: Each edge in T2 is used at most once for replacement.

postconditions.expression: all(is_tree(T1 - {(a, b)} + {(c, d)}) for a, b, c, d in protected_edges)
postconditions.description: Adding the replacement edge and removing the original edge results in a tree.
